questions.q: According to this wrap-up, what did the nine prior lessons actually teach, underneath the specific Azure CLI commands?
options: Memorizing every `az` command flag by heart
Transferable skills -- requirements clarification, scoping, deliberate provisioning, real validation, and clear communication -- that matter independent of the specific tool
How to pass a single certification exam
How to avoid ever using the Azure Portal
questions.explain: The CLI commands were the vehicle. The real, transferable skills -- clarifying requirements, scoping deliberately, validating by testing, communicating clearly -- are what actually mattered.

questions.q: Which of these was explicitly part of this Beginner project's scope, as built across Lessons 1-9?
options: A multi-region, auto-scaling deployment of the catalog app
A fully automated CI/CD pipeline for future code deployments
One VM running the catalog app, migrated images in Blob Storage, basic monitoring, and a documented, tested, presented cutover plan
Migrating every application Driftwood runs, not just the catalog app
questions.explain: The project stayed scoped to one app: images moved to Blob Storage, the app server moved to one VM, with basic monitoring, testing, documentation, and a presented cutover plan -- nothing more.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say scoping down was "as real a skill as knowing how to scope up"?
options: Because scoping down is always easier than scoping up
Because deliberately choosing what not to build, to match effort to the actual request, is a real engineering judgment call -- not a shortcut or a limitation to apologize for
Because Azure charges more for larger deployments
Because Priya explicitly forbade building anything more complex
questions.explain: Scope discipline -- deliberately choosing what to leave out -- is presented throughout this course as a genuine, valuable skill, not a compromise.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why doesn't finishing this project mean Driftwood's cloud needs are fully addressed?
options: Because the migration itself failed and needs to be redone

Because the business reasons behind this migration -- growing traffic, less tolerance for downtime, a team depending on these systems daily -- don't stop applying just because one app finished migrating
Because Azure requires a new resource group every month
Because Priya has already announced the company is moving away from Azure
questions.explain: One migrated app on one VM is a real first step, not a finish line -- the same pressures that justified this migration will keep applying as the business keeps growing.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about exactly what Driftwood's next cloud steps should look like?
options: It lays out a complete technical plan for the next project
It deliberately does not describe the specifics -- that's a separate project, not something to guess at in this wrap-up
It states that no further changes will ever be needed
It instructs Theo to immediately rebuild the catalog app as microservices
questions.explain: The wrap-up previews that growth is coming without describing what it specifically looks like -- that's intentionally left for a separate project to define.
